Initial reaction rates v (uM/min) of a purified enzyme were measured at substrate concentrations S (uM) (no inhibitor, I = 0). Each condition was measured in duplicate; rates carry additive measurement noise.

The data table has 16 rows with columns: S, v. Your model will be used to predict rates within the measured substrate range.

Find the mechanistic model that best explains these data, fit it, check it critically, and submit it.

content.thinking:
I'm checking whether the velocity against S looks linear at low S before it saturates, and comparing the v/S ratios at a few points. The ratio sits near 0.19–0.2 across S = 4, 10, and 20, so it reads as nearly linear with maybe slight curvature. The values near S = 0.5 and S = 1 are noisy and close to zero.

I'm working through the remaining points, which show the slope near 0.19 to 0.2 across the range, so the relationship looks linear with no saturation. I'm considering whether a Michaelis-Menten fit with a very large Km would look the same, but the data read as linear. Next I want to check the intercept and fit a through-origin least-squares slope.

Now I'm adding up the two replicate sums of S times v, getting a combined total of about 302.6. The sum of squared S across both replicates comes to 1564.5, so the through-origin slope works out to roughly 0.193. Checking the residuals, both replicates at S = 20 and S = 0.5 fall close to the linear prediction, so I'll go with the linear rate model at k ≈ 0.193.
